issues.where: the far and right walls of the pit
issues.what: The target's curved, stacked mineral bands wrap around the cavity and meet the right wall. Here several thick shelves jut out and terminate abruptly against a broad, nearly bare vertical wall, so the pit reads as a different formation.
issues.fix: Carry narrower rounded bands around the right-hand curve at several depths, anchoring them into the dark wall and breaking them only locally.

issues.where: the main red plant at center and its upper-right crown
issues.what: The canopy peaks lower and farther left, leaving a large gap where the target's tallest fronds fill the upper center-right. The foliage hangs in dark stringy curtains instead of sweeping in lifted, tapering red sprays.
issues.fix: Raise and extend the crown rightward, and shape the descending sprays into irregular outward arcs with fine branching tips.

issues.where: the left edge and lower foreground
issues.what: The plant is much larger and more frame-filling, with near-black curtains reaching into the center and running off the bottom. The target leaves the opening mostly visible and frames it with a soft wet ledge across the lower left rather than a bright rock lip at lower right.
issues.fix: Pull the left sprays back toward the upper-left edge, leave more of the pit unobstructed, and bring the soft near ledge back into the lower-left foreground.

issues.where: the chasm and far rim on the right
issues.what: The hard near edge and huge pale slabs make an exposed stepped ravine. The target has a softer dark drop, a flatter far rim and a recessed pale band, with little rock visible through the low vapor.
issues.fix: Pull the exposed slabs down and back, re-form the recessed band under the far rim, and let depth of field and ascending vapor hide more of the drop.

issues.where: the animal on the upper-left flat
issues.what: A much larger apparent animal is mostly hidden behind the left fronds, leaving a towering neck silhouette; the target has one small, readable full-bodied long-necked animal with visible legs on the center-left flat.
issues.fix: Set the prominent animal farther back and right into the open gap, keeping its complete silhouette small, softly lit and visible against the wet flat.

issues.where: the steam from the lower cavity to the upper-left rim
issues.what: Broad bright diagonal veils wash over the upper opening and distant flat, while the target has dense, irregular billows climbing mainly from the lower-left and center of the pit under a clearer rim.
issues.fix: Concentrate layered turbulent vapor low in the cavity, break up the diagonal beams, and keep the rim and waterline clearer.

issues.where: the lighting and air from the left sun to the upper-right ridge
issues.what: A hard visible sun, nearly black foreground strands and an even gray-beige veil flatten the scene. In the target the upper-left light blooms warmer through the plants, isolated vapor plumes rise, and the far ridge fades behind them.
issues.fix: Diffuse the sun into a warmer left-hand bloom, let that light penetrate the red canopy, and replace the uniform veil with separated backlit plumes and softer distance falloff.

issues.where: the skyline and wet flats above the pit rim
issues.what: The rim crowds the top edge, leaving a shallow muted strip of flat. The target shows more wet ground receding behind a lower irregular rim, with a bright gold reflection path and several more legible small animals with reflected legs.
issues.fix: Give the wet flats more image height, restore broken gold reflections, and separate a few small full-bodied silhouettes from the haze with readable legs and reflections.

issues.where: the exposed right rim, shelves and wall face
issues.what: The pale ledges look chalky and the large wall has repetitive brown striations. The target has rounded wet cream-and-rust mineral flow, glossy streaks, droplets underneath and dark green-black rock between bands.
issues.fix: Add irregular mineral flow patterns, wet amber highlights, damp green-dark recesses and water trails falling from the rounded lips.

issues.where: the center ledges and lower-right rock pile
issues.what: Loose stones are spread over several ledges and piled on the near right, with a small stone appearing detached beside the wall. The target instead emphasizes a compact cluster of large fallen blocks resting on a mid-right band with more open depth below.
issues.fix: Bed the main angular blocks into a single visible mid-right ledge, pare back the near-right rubble and give every loose stone convincing contact.

issues.where: the base of the main plant and the lower ledge
issues.what: The base is a faceted brown bulb perched on a broad pitted bench. The target has moist branching roots embedded between rounded stones on a sloping wet ledge, with puddled glints and small pale debris.
issues.fix: Merge irregular fleshy roots into the rock, restore the sloping layered ledge and add wet channels, pebbles and sparse pale debris around the root bed.

issues.where: the center and left plant strands and their tips
issues.what: Thin wiry hairs, dark knots and detached-looking white drops replace the target's more translucent, wet copper-red fibres with gold glints and droplets visibly hanging from the tips.
issues.fix: Vary fibre thickness and branching, give the strands a moist translucent red sheen and attach tapering drops to the lit tips.

issues.where: the foreground red fronds and far-rim growth
issues.what: The foreground strands are coarser, straighter and more black-to-bright-red than the target's copper-lit wet sprays. The broken rim also lacks the target's distinct small rust-red tufts around center-left and center-right.
issues.fix: Use softer copper edge light and irregular wet branching on the near foliage, and add sparse low tufts to the far rim.
